slides.label: The news
slides.text: *Frances Tiafoe* clinched his first spot at the *ATP Finals* when Ben Shelton beat Tommy Paul in Paris. Turin, *November 15 to 22*.

slides.label: The room

slides.label: The season
slides.text: A *Halle title*. Finals in *Acapulco and Cincinnati*. A *US Open semifinal* run through Medvedev. Career-high *No. 8*.

slides.label: Where he started
slides.text: His parents fled *Sierra Leone's civil war*. His father helped build the *Junior Tennis Champions Center* in Maryland, then became its *custodian*.

slides.label: The court
slides.text: Frances and his twin brother *Franklin* grew up practically living there. *The court he trained on was the one his father kept clean.*

slides.text: Tennis was built for families who could afford it. Tiafoe came in *through the side door*. Now he walks into the *most exclusive room* in the sport.

yt_title: Frances Tiafoe ATP Finals Debut: From Maintenance Room to Turin
caption_instagram:
Frances Tiafoe is going to the ATP Finals for the first time. 🎾

Only eight men qualify for tennis's season-ending championship in Turin, November 15 to 22. Tiafoe clinched his spot when Ben Shelton beat Tommy Paul in Paris.

He earned it: a Halle title, finals in Acapulco and Cincinnati, a US Open semifinal run through Medvedev and a career-high No. 8 ranking.

And the story behind it: his parents fled Sierra Leone's civil war. His father helped build the Junior Tennis Champions Center in Maryland, then became its custodian. Frances and his twin brother grew up practically living there.

caption_facebook:
Frances Tiafoe has qualified for the ATP Finals for the first time. The eight-player season finale runs November 15 to 22 in Turin, and Tiafoe clinched his place when Ben Shelton beat Tommy Paul at the Paris Masters.

His 2026: a Halle title, finals in Acapulco and Cincinnati, a US Open semifinal and a career-high No. 8 ranking.

His parents came to the U.S. from Sierra Leone, escaping the civil war. His father worked on the crew that built the Junior Tennis Champions Center in College Park, Maryland, and stayed on as its custodian. That is where Frances learned the game.
caption_linkedin:
Frances Tiafoe just qualified for the ATP Finals, the eight-player championship that closes the tennis season.

His path is one of the great stories in sports. His parents left Sierra Leone during its civil war. His father helped build the Junior Tennis Champions Center in Maryland and became its custodian, and Frances trained there from childhood without the usual fees. This year he won Halle, reached two more finals and a US Open semifinal, and climbed to No. 8 in the world.

Talent is everywhere. Access is not. Programs that open the door change who ends up in the room.
